source.publication: 2025 DR 0104 Booklet (Colorado Individual Income Tax), DR 0104 and DR 0104AD
source.section: DR 0104AD line 4 / line 6 Pension and Annuity Subtraction (PDF p.18-19 Line 4 bullets; p.19-20 Line 6; DR 0104AD p.1 lines 4 and 6), second bullet: '$20,000 minus any amount entered on line 3'; DR 0104AD line 3 / line 5 Social Security Benefits (PDF p.18 Line 3; p.19 Line 5; DR 0104AD p.1 lines 3 and 5); DR 0104 lines 1, 10-13 (PDF p.8, p.10); tax table PDF p.34-35

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 20,000.00 + IRA distribution (you) 25,000.00 + taxable Social Security 10,200.00 = 55,200.00. Taxable Social Security on gross benefits 12,000.00 (you): federal SS worksheet (given): half of benefits 6,000.00 + other income 45,000.00 = 51,000.00; less 25,000.00 = 26,000.00; line 11 = 17,000.00; line 13 = half of smaller of 26,000.00 and 9,000.00 = 4,500.00; line 14 = 4,500.00; line 15 = 85% x 17,000.00 = 14,450.00; line 16 = 18,950.00; 85% of benefits = 10,200.00; taxable Social Security = 10,200.00. Federal taxable income = 55,200.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 39,450.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). DR 0104 line 1 federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15) 39,450.00; lines 2-9 additions 0.00 (no state income tax addback, no other-state bond interest; federal AGI 55,200.00 is not over 300,000, so no line 4 deduction addback); line 10 subtotal 39,450.00. DR 0104AD: Line 3 (primary taxpayer, age 63, 55-64): federal AGI (DR 0104 line 34) 55,200.00 does not exceed 75,000.00 (single), so the entire taxable Social Security 10,200.00 (better than the 20,000-limited subtraction, smaller of 10,200.00 and 20,000.00 = 10,200.00). Line 4 (primary taxpayer, age 63, at least 55 but not yet 65): taxable pension, annuity and IRA income 25,000.00; limit 20,000.00 minus line 3 10,200.00 = 9,800.00; subtraction = smaller of 25,000.00 and 9,800.00 = 9,800.00. Line 22 subtotal = 20,000.00; DR 0104 line 11 = 20,000.00. Line 12 Colorado taxable income = 39,450.00 - 20,000.00 = 19,450.00. Line 13 tax = 4.4% x 19,450.00 = 855.80 (the tax table row over 19,400.00 but not over 19,500.00, PDF p.34, gives 856.00; expected keeps the formula figure). No credits claimed: 0.00. Colorado income tax 855.80. co_ss_55_64_full is tested here on the below side of its 75,000 threshold too (federal AGI 55,200.00).
accepted_approximations: Tax is figured on the exact income at 4.4%; below 50,000 the booklet uses the tax table, which taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds to the dollar.

The pension cap is reduced by each person's taxable Social Security (the record's line 3 or line 5 subtraction). That equals the printed rule whenever the Social Security subtraction is the person's full taxable benefit, and also when it is limited to 20,000 (the 55-64 pension cap is then used up either way). How a joint return's taxable Social Security (Form 1040 line 6b) is split between spouses is left to a Department publication not in the sources; the projection splits it the way the household's facts do.
